chunks: And upon you be peace, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. As for what follows:

Know, O my son, that if your Lord had a partner, His messengers would have come to you, and you would have seen the signs of His dominion and authority, and known His actions and attributes. But He is One God as He has described Himself. No one disputes with Him in His dominion. He never ceases and has never ceased. He is the First before things, without a beginning, and the Last after things, without an end. He is too great for His lordship to be encompassed by the heart or the eye. So when you know this, do as one like you should do, in the smallness of his stature, the littleness of his power, the abundance of his weakness, and the great need of his Lord, in seeking His obedience, fearing His punishment, and dreading His anger, for He has not commanded you except for good, nor forbidden you except for evil.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of God mentioned in Imam Ali's instructions to Hasan in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from the Instructions for Hasan, delivered after the Battle of Siffin, serves as a profound theological treatise on Tawhid al-Dhat (Oneness of Essence), asserting that God’s absolute sovereignty precludes any partner or rival. It bridges metaphysical transcendence with practical ethics, urging Hasan to recognize his inherent human limitation (‘ajz) and need (ghina) to cultivate humility, fear, and gratitude in worship.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Know O my child, if there had been a partner with your Lord, his messengers too should have come to you and you would have seen signs of his authority and power and have known his deeds and qualities. But He is only One God as He has described Himself. No one can dispute with Him in His authority. He is from ever and will be for ever. He is before all things without any beginning. He will remain after all things without any end. He is far too great to have His divinity proved by the encompassing heart or eye. When you have understood this then you should do what is done by him who is like you by way of his low position, his lack of authority, his increasing incapability, and his great need of his Lord for seeking His obedience, fearing His chastisement and apprehending His anger, because He does not command you save for virtue and does not refrain you save from evil.
